topic: UK welfare fraud and error trends

claims.claim: Overall welfare fraud and error rose from 3.1% of spending in 2019-20 to 4.3% during 2020-21 and 2021-22, then fell to 3.2%.
Universal Credit fraud and error rose from 9.4% of UC spending in 2019-20 to 14.7% in 2021-22, then fell to 8.5% in 2025-26.
The Covid cohort fraud and error rate was 25.8% of spending in 2020-21 and fell to 8.9% in 2025-26.
claims.section: Executive summary paragraph 1.4; Recent trends paragraph 2.8 and Chart 2.2

claims.claim: The Covid cohort means UC cases joining between 14 March 2020 and 27 February 2021.

OBR says the initially high Covid-cohort rate is likely primarily explained by pandemic operational easements, including relaxed claim checks and suspension of minimum-income-floor and gainfully-self-employed checks; the shock also increased self-employed UC cases.
OBR plans to remove the previous assumption that the underlying propensity for UC fraud and error rises each forecast year.
Fraud and error data come from sampling exercises, evidence on underlying drivers is limited, and conclusions are uncertain.

interpretation: The pandemic-period spike was concentrated in Universal Credit and especially among claims entering during the first pandemic year. Rates subsequently fell close to or below pre-pandemic levels, but OBR presents causal explanations and future judgements as uncertain.
